Logitech’s MX Master 3S has been a desk favorite for years, and the Bluetooth Edition just hit its lowest price yet. The Logitech MX Master 3S Bluetooth Edition in Graphite is $72.19 on Amazon, down from its $99.99 list price. That’s $28 off, a 28% discount, and a new all-time low.

This version uses the same MX Master 3S hardware but leaves the Logi Bolt USB receiver out of the box. It connects over Bluetooth instead, which suits most modern laptops, and it can still pair with a Bolt receiver later if you want one.

What makes the Logitech MX Master 3S so popular is how well it handles everyday work. The 8,000 DPI sensor tracks on almost any surface, including glass at least 4mm thick, and the clicks are 90% quieter than the previous MX Master 3. The MagSpeed electromagnetic scroll wheel can fly through up to 1,000 lines per second, then switch to precise line-by-line scrolling.

It’s built for multitaskers too. Easy-Switch lets you pair up to three devices and jump between them with a button, and a full charge over USB-C lasts up to 70 days. It works with Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, and more.

With a 4.6-star rating on Amazon, it’s an easy upgrade for a home office or a thoughtful gift for anyone who spends their day at a desk.

Google’s most affordable noise canceling earbuds are back at their best price. The Pixel Buds 2a are $99 on Amazon, which is $30 off the $129 list price, a 23% discount. That matches the lowest price they’ve ever sold for, and every color is included.

You get active noise canceling and a Transparency mode, so you can block out a noisy commute or let the world back in with a tap. The earbuds run on Google’s Tensor A1 chip and weigh just 4.7g each, which makes them easy to wear for hours at a time.

Battery life is strong for earbuds at this price. You get up to seven hours from the buds with noise canceling on, or 10 hours with it off, and the case stretches that to 20 or 27 hours in total. The buds are IP54 rated against dust and splashes, and the case is IPX4, so a rainy walk or a sweaty workout is no problem.

They’re a natural match for Pixel phones, but the Pixel Buds 2a work with any Android phone or iPhone over Bluetooth. They also hold a 4.4-star rating on Amazon from more than 700 reviews.

This price has come around a few times this year, and it’s a good one to grab whether you want a pair for yourself or a gift for someone on your list this Black Friday season.

items.body: Apple today shared a fun ad highlighting the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery, which offers the longest battery life ever in an iPhone. In the spot, a cyclops toy comes to life and becomes enamored with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max. The toy takes photos, plays games, uses apps, listens to music, captures videos, makes calls, watches TV, and uses the flashlight for shadow puppets. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts through all of it, remaining at half charge when the cyclops's battery dies and the toy falls asleep. Apple's ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts up to 30 hours in "typical use," which is based on median iPhone usage. The metric includes messages, photo taking, music, social app use, streaming, games, browsing, and navigation. The device lasts for up to 40 hours when streaming video, and up to 45 hours when watching downloaded videos. items.title: $799 Smart Glasses Promise Vision Pro-Style Controls in a 45g Frame
items.summary: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25…
items.body: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery. Savage highlights the bulky hardware currently required for Apple's spatial computing experience, although Orrorin offers substantially fewer capabilities. Savage says small pinches performed at the user's side control the interface without a ring, wristband, or controller. Eye tracking makes the display fade when the wearer looks away, rather than selecting interface elements as it does on Vision Pro. That also distinguishes Orrorin from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, which costs the same $799 but has a screen for only the right eye and requires a Neural Band wristband for gesture control. Standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses have no displays. Orrorin lacks positional tracking and spatial mapping , so it cannot anchor virtual windows in a room like Vision Pro. Orrorin is the first product from Savage Technology, co-founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, and remains in engineering validation for now. The company is currently targeting developers with third-party apps and interaction with AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Apple is expected to launch its first smart glasses next year , although the initial model reportedly will not have displays, instead offering speakers, microphones, and Siri integration. Orrorin reservations start at $29 toward the $799 price. Savage estimates shipments will begin in March 2027 for Founder Edition buyers and May 2027 for Early Bird buyers. items.title: Apple Has an iPhone Notifications Problem
items.summary: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to s…
items.body: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to send push notifications for promotions or direct marketing purposes, but only if users have "explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed" in the app, and so long as the app provides a method "for a user to opt out from receiving such messages." The guideline, in part: Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app's UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Unfortunately, there are some examples of apps ignoring this guideline. On my iPhone in Canada, there are several apps that send me push notifications containing promotions without offering a way to opt out of these promotion-specific notifications, such as Cineplex, McDonald's, and Wendy's. Canadian food delivery app Skip does offer a setting to turn off promotional notifications, but it has continued to send them to me long after I opted out. Do you have any iOS apps that don't respect your promo notification settings or don't let you turn off promo notifications as Apple requires? Let me know for a MacRumors story! Example: @SkipCanada sends me promo notifications long after I turned off that option in their app. https://t.co/NIhXEUghJ6 — Joe Rossignol (@rsgnl) November 25, 2026 A few MacRumors readers informed us that after they turned off DoorDash notifications for offers specifically and then place a delivery order, the app will prompt users to re-enable notifications so they "never miss an order update," even though they still have notifications enabled for order updates. items.summary: Nothing says it features the company’s ‘best in-ear audio ever.’
items.body:

Nothing Ear note teaser shows off its earbuds and unique charging case

Nothing says it features the company’s ‘best in-ear audio ever.’

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 11:29 AM ET

•

•

Nothing

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Following multiple previews of the Nothing Ear note, the company has shared a teaser video of the earbuds.

• We’re getting a closer look at the Ear note’s key elements, including the large charging case, the earbuds themselves, and a USB-C port, among other details.

• The Ear note will break cover on December 8, with the company claiming it will offer “best in-ear audio ever.”

Nothing recently shared more details on the Ear note, a pair of earbuds with a charging case that doubles as an AI audio recorder. The company has now shared a video detailing its new hardware ahead of the December 8 launch.

In a video posted to YouTube and social media platforms, Nothing offers a good look at the Ear note’s design from multiple angles, highlighting the charging case’s hardware buttons, a USB-C port, and more.

While the video offers a decent look at the earbuds and the charging case/AI recorder, the description walks through some features and calls it Nothing’s “best in-ear audio ever.”

A Bloomberg report earlier this week revealed a bulk of the Ear note’s features, with CEO Carl Pei noting at the time that this is the company’s first step toward “building a hardware context layer for AI.” Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis shared a similar sentiment shortly after the video teaser was published.

Based on what we know so far, the Ear note will record calls through both the earbuds and the charging case, with the latter featuring a couple of handy buttons to start recording instantly. The companion app can turn all recordings into summaries and transcripts, with support for Nothing’s AI voice assistant alongside other AI agents.

Pricing information is currently unavailable, and that’s unlikely to change until the company announces the Ear note on December 8.

Nothing released the Ear 3a earlier this year with audio and call recording support. However, the Ear note takes it a step further with its charging case that serves as a standalone audio recorder.

We’re also eager to learn whether the Ear note’s audio performance holds up against the best earbuds in the segment. The company saying this is its best in-ear audio product is certainly encouraging news.

items.title: Apple Has iPads Running macOS Internally, Says Gurman
items.summary: Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads. Speaking on his latest Power On podcast , Gurman said there is "no work being done to consume…
items.body: Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads. Speaking on his latest Power On podcast , Gurman said there is "no work being done to consumerize macOS on the iPad." Rather, Apple will continue to bring Mac features and apps like Final Cut to iPadOS piece by piece. Gurman also argued that per-operating-system EU regulation gives Apple an incentive to keep distinct systems for each device. Apple recently dismissed merging iPadOS and macOS. With Black Friday kicking off this week, plus new products, software updates, and new smart home accessories running into December, there's more on the way from Apple before the end of 2026, so be sure to stick around. Below, we've rounded up what's still coming, along with one date in particular that's worth watching if you're a holiday shopper. Black Friday – November 27: Not a product launch unfortunately, but a date likely worth marking. Apple's annual four-day shopping event runs from Friday, November 27 through Monday, November 30, with gift cards worth up to $300 offered with eligible purchases. Apple is also offering new and qualified returning subscribers the Apple TV streaming service for $6.99 per month for six months, with that deal available until November 30. Our Black Friday roundup will be tracking all the deals. (PRODUCT)RED AirPods Max 2 and HomePod mini 2 – expected December 1: Apple plans to release (PRODUCT)RED versions of the existing AirPods Max 2 and HomePod mini 2 on or around Tuesday, December 1, which is World AIDS Day, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman. The new color is expected to be the only change. Apple is also releasing a red Wrist Strap for AirPods Pro and a red Sport Band for the Apple Watch. App Store Awards – expected December: Apple named this year's finalists on November 18 , and the winners are expected in the coming weeks. Last year, Apple announced the winners on December 4 , so a similar early-December date looks likely this year. Apple Music Replay – expected December: The full 2026 Replay recap is likely to arrive around the same time as last year's, when the full version became available on December 2 , with your top songs, artists, and listening stats for the year. iOS 27.3 – December: Apple says iOS 27.3 will be released to the public in December , though it hasn't given a date.
